title: Linear recurrence from an index on
statement:
Let $K$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $(c_n)_{n\geq0}$ a sequence of elements of $K$. Let $m\geq0$ and $d\geq1$ be integers and $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}\in K$. The sequence $(c_n)$ *satisfies the linear recurrence of order $d$ with coefficients $a_0,\ldots,a_{d-1}$ from the index $m$ on* if
$$
c_{n+d}+a_{d-1}c_{n+d-1}+\cdots+a_0c_n=0\qquad(n\geq m),
$$
that is, $c_{n+d}=-\sum_{i=0}^{d-1}a_ic_{n+i}$ for every integer $n\geq m$. For $m=0$ the relation holds for every $n\geq0$.

source.place: Ch. II, §27, proof of Lemma 27.9, p. 157 (quoting Bourbaki, Algèbre, IV.5, Exercise 3(a): f lies in k(t) iff its coefficients satisfy a linear relation λ_1a_n+…+λ_ra_{n+r-1}=0 for all n≥d; stated, not proved)
